General Education Outcomes
Tags: courses
Short Description: Undergraduate students must complete at least 3 credits addressing each of the 12 General Education Student Learning Outcomes, organized across four areas: Knowledge, Competencies, Responsibilities, and Integrate & Apply.
General Education Outcomes

The General Education program will assess student exposure to twelve Student Learning Outcomes in four areas:
A. Build knowledge of diverse peoples and cultures and of the natural and physical world.
(A1) STEM Disciplines (A2) Social & Behavioral Sciences (A3) Humanities (A4) Art & Design
B. Develop intellectual and interdisciplinary competencies for academic and lifelong learning.
(B1) Write Effectively (B2) Communicate Effectively (B3) Mathematical, Statistical, or Computational Strategies (B4) Information Literacy
C. Exercise individual and social responsibilities.
(C1) Civic Knowledge & Responsibilies (C2) Global Responsibility (C3) Diversity & Inclusion
D. Integrate and apply these abilities and capacities, adapting them to new settings, questions, and responsibilities to lay the foundation for lifelong learning.
(D1) Integrate & Apply

General Education courses may assess one or two Student Learning Outcomes in the following configurations:
Knowledge (A) and Competency (B)
Knowledge (A) and Responsibility (C)
Competency (B) and Competency (B)
Competency (B) and Responsibility (C)
Integration (D) and Competency (B)
Integration (D) and Responsibility (C)

S/U Only
Tags: courses
Short Description: A grading method in which student performance is recorded as S (Satisfactory) or U (Unsatisfactory) rather than a letter grade.
S/U Only

Certain courses do not lend themselves to precise grading. For these courses, only S (satisfactory) or U (unsatisfactory) is given to all students enrolled. S/U courses are labeled as such in the course descriptions in this catalog. S/U courses are not counted as courses taken under the Pass-Fail option.
D1 is the only General Education outcome that can be graded using S/U or Letter Grades. All other outcomes must be graded by Letter Grades.

Program Modification Proposal Walkthrough
Program Modification Proposal Walkthrough
This page is under construction
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a Course Modification Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Related toolkit entry: Specialization Modification Proposal Walkthrough

Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
How the Curriculum Process Works
Related toolkit entry: How the Curriculum Process Works
Approval Calendar
Related toolkit entry: Approval Calendar

You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
Kuali Basics
Related toolkit entry: Kuali Basics

If you are unsure which type applies to your proposal, review the examples below.
Table columns: If you want to… | Use…
If you want to…: Change the requirements of a major or degree program | Use…: Program modification proposal
If you want to…: Change the requirements to a major or degree program, and it’s specializations (options, tracks, sub-plans). | Use…: Program modification proposal and specialization modification proposal (one for each existing specialization that you want to change)
If you want to…: Change only the requirements of one specialization of a major or degree program | Use…: Specialization modification proposal
If you want to…: Create an Accelerated Online Version of an existing program | Use…: New program proposal
If you want to…: Change the title of a program while teaching-out the original name. | Use…: New program proposal - to create new title Program modification proposal - to suspend admission to old title
If you want to…: Create a new program with specializations | Use…: New program proposal and new specialization(s) proposal(s)
If you want to…: Create a 4+1 Pathway | Use…: New specialization proposal, inherited to the Bachelors degree.
If you want to…: Create an ABM program | Use…: New specialization proposal, inherited to the Masters degree.

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Programs.
On the Programs page, use the search bar at the top to find the course you would like to modify. You can search by:
Degree Title (e.g., Bachelor of Music, or Bachelor of Arts)
Major Title (e.g., Environmental Arts & Humanities)
Keywords found in the description, or anywhere in the course form.
Once you locate the program, select it to open the current version
With the current program open, select Propose Changes in the upper-right corner of the window.
A window will appear prompting you to select Create a new version or Create a new revision. Always select Create a new version.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.
Select the applicable changes in the checkboxes/radio buttons.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program.
Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term with Modifications Select the term and year in which you anticipate the students will graduate with the changes proposed.
Credential Type This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Level This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Academic Calendar This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

Alternatively, you may propose a new program by cloning the existing program. This approach does not require Board of Trustees approval and is treated as a program modification. Creating a separate program allows students to be appropriately coded according to the academic calendar in which their program is offered (Traditional or Accelerated).
Program Locations Select all locations where the program will be offered.
College This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification Section of the proposal.
Department This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification section of the proposal.
CIP Code This field will already be populated.
If it is not populated, enter the program’s current CIP Code as listed on eCampus.
If you are changing the program’s CIP code, make sure Change CIP Code is selected from the Program Modification section of the proposal, and enter the new code in the space provided.

🔽 The following field will appear only if Change Academic Home is checked in the Program Modification section.
Upload Letter(s) of support from outgoing home college and/or department. Upload confirmation from the original department/college that they are in support of the program moving to a new academic home.
Is this interdisciplinary? This field will already be populated. The intent of this question is to identify whether the program is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen for Is this interdisciplinary?
Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Degree or Major is chosen for Credential Type.
Degree This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Major is chosen for Credential Type.
Major This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change name of major, minor, or certificate from the Program Modification section.

Academic Program Title This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change name of major, minor, or certificate from the Program Modification section.
See Academic Program Title for catalog formatting.
Related toolkit entry: Academic Program Title
Program Description This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected any of the following changes from the Program Modification section:
Change name of major, minor, or certificate
Change program description
Change total number of credits required for graduation
Change core courses
Change elective courses
Change other program requirements
Suspend or Reopen Program
See Program Description for catalog formatting.
Related toolkit entry: Program Description
Admission Requirements This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change admission requirements from the Program Modification section.
See Admission Requirements for criteria
Related toolkit entry: Admission Requirements
Total program credits Enter the total number of credits required to earn the credential.

Total core course credits Enter the total number of credits required for core courses.
Total elective course credits Enter the total number of credits required for elective courses.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Level is Undergraduate or Dual.
Total general education course credits Enter the total number of required General Education credits.
List the name(s) and title(s) of the individual(s) responsible for administering the program. Enter the name of the program director, department chair, or other individual responsible for administering the program.

🔽 This section will appear only if one of the options under Change Program Modality is chosen from the Program Modification section.
Are all required resources (faculty, staff, instructional equipment, etc.) currently available for this program? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if No is selected for the question above.
Describe the additional resources needed and provide a rationale.
Will the change in program modality offer any new assistantships, scholarships, and/or fellowships? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
List any new available assistantships, scholarships and/or fellowships.
Supporting Documentation Optional.
Describe how program resources, equipment, and technology comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state disability statutes.
For the proposed modality change, provide the number of currently enrolled students and explain how the change will impact their ability to complete the program and how they will be supported throughout the transition.
Will this change require additional funding, resources, or personnel?

🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the anticipated additional funding, resources, or personnel required to support this modality change.
Attach supporting documentation Optional.

Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
